text:
Casey: Quick situation - my dependent turns 26 next week but is finishing a semester abroad and has a letter from the university saying theyre enrolled full-time through the end of the term (returns in 6 weeks). Do I need to remove them immediately on their 26th birthday or can they stay on Redwood until the semester ends? Also any docs I should prepare?
Nora (People Ops): Congrats to them on finishing the term! Policy: dependent coverage ends at the end of the month they turn 26 unless they meet a qualifying exception. Full-time student status can sometimes qualify for extension, but it depends on plan rules and whether the student is a "dependent child" under our policy.
Casey: Hmm ok. The uni letter explicitly states full-time enrollment and gives dates. Will that help?
BenefitsBot: KB: https://redwood.example.com/kb/benefits/student-dependent-rules - outlines acceptable student enrollment proofs and timeline for review.
Sam (Benefits): Upload the university enrollment letter / transcript showing full-time status + passport/ID and a short note "Casey - dependent 26 extension request". We can process a student-extension review. If approved, coverage can be extended to the documented term end date, but we need it BEFORE the 26th ideally.
Casey: What if I miss that and they age out, can we COBRA back in?
Sam (Benefits): If they age out (loss of dependent status), they qualify for a COBRA election as an event-triggered beneficiary. COBRA is separate from dependent enrollment and must be elected within 60 days of the qualifying event. COBRA premiums are usually full cost (employee+employer share), so its more expensive.
Raj (Payroll): Note on payroll/proration: if we process an extension that keeps them covered into the next month, premiums will continue as usual. If we have to remove and COBRA is later elected, payroll won't retrospectively cover COBRA premiums  COBRA billing is handled by our benefits vendor. If we owe a refund because of retro removal, Payroll issues credits in the next pay cycle once Benefits confirms the change.
Casey: Tight timeline - their birthday is 3 days away. I uploaded the uni letter and a screenshot of their student portal. What should I expect next?
Nora (People Ops): Case created #BP-9911. Benefits will review within 2 business days. If we can approve an extension, well set the dependent eligibility to the term end date and notify Payroll. If not approved, we'll send COBRA election info and removal date.
Sam (Benefits): Also check whether the foreign university term qualifies under plan rules (some plans require accredited institutions). If we need translation or an apostille for the letter, we'll ask, but usually an official enrollment letter is enough.
Casey: Thanks all, fingers crossed. Appreciate the speedy help. :crossed_fingers:
